headline: A regional research office says Asia is among the economies most at risk if the AI boom turns into a correction.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a regional research body warns of a possible AI correction; the lead economist says warning signals are "not grave yet".
importance_line: Workers and exporters across East and South-east Asia could be hit if AI spending falls back, but the research office itself says the warning signs are not yet serious.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by The Business Times, that the Asean+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO), a regional research body covering South-east Asia plus China, Japan and South Korea, says Asia is among the economies most exposed to a sharp fall in the AI boom. It estimates that a slowdown in AI-related demand could cut as much as 1.5 percentage points from the region's 2027 growth, currently forecast at 4.1 per cent.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked; text read in The Business Times (Singapore), which carries the Bloomberg report (BLOOMBERG credit at the end). Original: AMRO report published Monday 5 Oct 2026. Original Bloomberg link kept as url.
